summary: A Cook County, Illinois jury returned a $28.7M wrongful-death verdict (~$29.6M in 2024 USD) against a Chicago-area hospital for medical negligence.
source_citation: Reported via Lubin & Meyer / TopVerdict roundup of 2023-2024 largest verdicts (lubinandmeyer.com/news/largest-verdicts-settlements.html) — verdict total documented but full party/court detail not independently confirmed in primary filings.

summary: Federal jury awarded $26.75M total (~$28.8M in 2024 USD; $2.75M compensatory + $24M punitive) for the death of Cindy Lou Hill from a ruptured intestine after denied jail medical care, a Section 1983 deliberate-indifference case later capped at a 4:1 punitive ratio.

MTA/Metro-North reached a ~$182M global settlement (~$182M in 2024 USD) for the 2015 Valhalla train-crossing crash resolving five passenger deaths plus dozens of injuries, with per-death payouts ranging roughly $4M to $35M after the jury assigned Metro-North 71% liability.
label_raw: ~$182M global settlement (five deaths plus injuries; ~$4M-$35M per death)
source_citation: Gair Gair Conason (PR Newswire), prnewswire.com/news-releases/...-182-million-metro-north-settlement... ; ABC7 NY, abc7ny.com/post/mta-settlement-worth-182m-reached-2015-metro-north-...

summary: US DOT regulatory value of a statistical life used to value one prevented transportation fatality in benefit-cost analysis, headline ~$13.7M for 2024 (cited as $13.2M in 2023 dollars), ~$11.6-13.6M in 2024 USD.
source_citation: US DOT, "Revised Departmental Guidance on Valuation of a Statistical Life in Economic Analysis," transportation.gov/office-policy/transportation-policy/revised-departmental-guidance-on-valuation-of-a-statistical-life-in-economic-analysis ; DHS/USCG VSL memo 9 May 2024, dco.uscg.mil/Portals/9/VSL%202024%209May24%20FINAL%20for%20DIST.pdf

summary: US EPA central value of a statistical life used to value one prevented fatality in air and water benefit-cost analysis, base $7.4M in 2006 dollars updated to the analysis year (~$11.6M in 2024 USD).
source_citation: US EPA, "Mortality Risk Valuation," epa.gov/environmental-economics/mortality-risk-valuation — "central estimate of $7.4 million ($2006), updated to the year of the analysis." (See also EPA final VSL guidance, Fed. Reg. 89 FR, 18 Apr 2024, doc. 2024-08300.)

summary: US HHS central value of a statistical life used to value a prevented fatality in regulatory impact analyses for drug, food, and health rules, ~$11.5M in 2023 dollars (~$11.8M in 2024 USD; range $5.9M-$17.0M).
source_citation: HHS/ASPE, "HHS Standard Values for Regulatory Analysis, 2025" (Feb 2025), aspe.hhs.gov/sites/default/files/documents/639756a60fbe7e51786bcec176ad52f1/Standard-RIA-Values-2025.pdf — "central estimate of $11.5 million … in 2023 dollars and 2023 income year."

summary: Texas jury awarded $860M total (~$890M in 2024 USD) for the single wrongful death of Kiersten Smith, killed when a tower crane collapsed onto her apartment, finding developer Greystar grossly negligent with a large punitive component.
label_raw: $860M total verdict (Williams v. Bigge Crane & Rigging / Greystar)
